slides.title:
How to
remember
what you
*read.*
slides.sub: Study one page before you start any non-fiction book. It takes a few minutes.

slides.body: Weeks after you finish a non-fiction book, you can give the gist and one or two points. Not much more.
slides.punch: You remember a _feeling_ about the book, not the book itself.
slides.foot: The fix happens before you read →

slides.title:
Read the
*structure*
first.
slides.body: Before page one, spend a few minutes on the contents page. Learn the chapter titles by heart if you can. Guess what each will say, then read to check.
slides.note: An old idea: Mortimer Adler described it in _How to Read a Book_ (1940).

slides.title:
Why it works:
ideas need *shelves.*
slides.quote: Without the structure, new ideas pile up. With it, each one has a place to go.
